newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen mostly steady - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen mostly steady - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen mostly steady, instances $0.50 per cwt higher, on support from light hog marketings Monday and expected light runs again Tuesday, livestock dealers said.
The light marketings were prompting increased competition among packer buyers for available hogs, sources said.

Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota top prices for hogs delivered to plant were seen at $52.50 to $53.50, sources there said. Illinois top prices at plants could range $53.00 to $53.50 and Indiana/Ohio top values were seen in a range of $52.00 to $52.50, sources in those areas said.
Support from the light marketings could be short-lived, however, amid concern that pork prices may be poised to slip further after Friday's declines, some sources said.
"There's a lot of concern that pork prices could get whacked by the end of the day," a hog buyer in southern Minnesota said.

Fresh pork prices at midday were not well tested, with heavy hams quoted steady, trimmings mostly steady and pork bellies not established, USDA reported. There were 14 loads of pork cuts and 11 loads of trimmed/processed pork sold as of midday, USDA said.
